params.body:
The site now follows the structure in the website feedback (Portal mail:6): landing page, Infrastructure, Services, How we work, News and insights.

Closes #3
Closes #4
Closes #7
Closes #8
Closes #9
Closes #10

Part of #5 (the self-assessment exists; where the answers end up is still open). #6 stays open: the landing page keeps the team as its trust signal, and there are no testimonials.

## What changed

**Navigation (#3).** The menu is Infrastructure, Services, How we work, News and insights. `networks.html` forwards to `infrastructure.html#role`. Verifiable AI is no longer in the menu: it is the volition example on Services and stays linked from there and from the footer.

**Landing page (#4).**
- The central message is the opening of the old Services page, verbatim: "Your access point to trusted issuance, verification and records." with its sub line.
- One new line under it: "Based in Belgium, working with organisations across Europe."
- One button, to the self-assessment. The hero proof (purchase order, invoice, contract) stays.
- Below the hero: three signposts (Infrastructure, Services, How we work), the regulatory-window band (its button also leads to the self-assessment), the team, the latest posts and contact.
- Moved off the landing page: the features, the ISBE layers, the four service tabs, who we work with, and the FAQ.

**Infrastructure (#7).** A new page, in the order the feedback asks for:
1. The old landing hero as its opener ("Your trusted gateway to Europe's regulated blockchain infrastructure").
2. Regulated blockchains: the features and the ISBE layer diagram.
3. ISBE and EBSI and Bextrust's role in each.
4. What we solve (access, knowledge, tools).
5. The four infrastructure services (node hosting, trust registry, BaaS, QEL) as the tabbed block that was on the landing page.

The trust model is not on the page yet: there is no text for it.

**Services (#8).** The page is rebuilt around verification, validation and volition.
- Each section opens with the definition from the handbook introduction attached to the mail, verbatim.
- Each has an example, how we build it, and what it changes:
  - verification: a diploma issued in one batch and presented from an EUDI Wallet;
  - validation: a product passport with supply-chain checkpoints anchored on a schedule;
  - volition: an AI agent acting under a signed permission, linking to Verifiable AI.
- The examples follow the Bextrust service description (v2).
- The EAA and QEAA comparison stays, under verification. Who we work with moved here from the landing page.

**How we work (#9).** The billing lines follow the service description:
- a one-time setup fee set by complexity, and a monthly fee set by volume;
- in the Delegated model, Bextrust does everything except the signing, and the client keeps an approval right that cannot be bypassed;
- in Guided Self-Management, the client holds its own keys.

A short "How we price" section explains why the two fees are separate. No amounts are published: the rates in that document are working assumptions.

**News and insights (#10).** The blog page is renamed and takes the FAQ. The three posts whose sources were lost keep their body. Only their header, footer and breadcrumb are refreshed, so they show the new menu.

**Self-assessment (part of #5).** `assessment.html` has:
- the sector and the type of organisation;
- the five questions from the feedback, each with a low-to-high slider;
- the closing offer: "Book a free assessment. In 30 minutes, we map your current verification process and identify where you lose time, money or trust".

The button opens an e-mail to info@bextrust.be with the answers filled in. Nothing is stored or sent until the visitor sends that e-mail, so the privacy page does not change. Collecting the answers centrally, to see which sectors respond, needs a decision on where they are kept. That is why #5 stays open.

## Copy that changed or is new

Client copy was moved verbatim except in these places, so the review can check them.

**Legal presumption.** ISBE is not qualified yet. These moved texts said records carry a legal presumption today, and now say it applies once ISBE holds qualified ledger status:
- the FAQ answer on legal validity;
- the QEL tab "Legal standing";
- the qDLT feature card;
- the QTSP card under who we work with.

**New text**, written for this structure and flagged for review:
- the "Based in Belgium" line;
- the signpost cards;
- the Services hero;
- the one-line headings of the three Vs;
- the "What it changes" lines;
- the self-assessment intro;
- the two buttons "Check your verification in two minutes" and "Check where you stand".

**One definition to check.** The verification definition ("eliminating the need for trusted authorities") sits on the site of a trust provider. Is that the intended framing?

## How it was checked

- `python3 site/src/pages.py` builds every page, and a second run changes nothing.
- Every internal link and anchor in `site/build` resolves.
- The landing page, Infrastructure, Services, How we work, News and insights and the self-assessment were rendered at 1366 px and 390 px wide in headless Chromium, with no horizontal overflow.
- On phones the header still hides the menu below 900 px, as before. The signposts and the footer carry the links there.
params.title: Restructure the site into landing, Infrastructure, Services, How we work, News and insights
